'''Jacques Lucas''' (born 12 June 1937 in [[Carhaix-Plouguer]]) is Professor Emeritus at the [[University of Rennes 1]]. Jacques Lucas is a solids-based [[chemist]] who specializes in the discovery of new lenses, contributing to their analysis, knowledge of their optical properties and their use in various fields (telecommunications, night vision and in situ analysis in chemistry and medicine). He is a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Académie des sciences|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-L/jacques-lucas.html|publication-date=}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Jacques Lucas, Doctor of Science (1964), was appointed Professor at the University of Rennes in 1968. He is Professor Emeritus at the University of Rennes where he created and directed the Laboratory of Glass and Ceramics. He has spent his entire career at this university, which has included numerous visits abroad as a visiting professor in [[Tucson, Arizona|Tucson]], [[Kyoto]] and [[Shanghai]]. He has directed more than a hundred doctoral students and published more than four hundred articles in the field of solid chemistry and especially infrared transmitting glasses.<ref>{{cite web|title=Google Scholar|url=https://scholar.google.fr/scholar?start=130&q=jacques+lucas&hl=fr&as_sdt=0,5|publication-date=}}</ref>

== Scientific work ==
After a career devoted to the chemistry of certain types of solids belonging to the [[pyrochlore]] and fluorinated materials family, he began studying a new family of glasses, [[fluoride]] glasses.<ref>Lucas Jacques, Chanthanasinh Maydom, Poulain Marcel, Poulain Michel, Brun Pierre, Weber Marvin J., « Preparation and optical properties of neodymium fluorozirconate glasses », ''Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids'', (1978), 27(2), p. 273-38</ref><ref>Poulain Michel, Poulain Marcel, Lucas Jacques, Brun Pierre, « Fluoride glasses with zirconium tetrafluoride. Optical properties of a neodymium-doped glass », ''Materials Research Bulletin'', (1975), 10(4), p. 243-6</ref><ref>Phifer Carol, C.A Angell, Laval, J.P Lucas Jacques, « A structural model for prototypical fluorozirconate glass », ''Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids'', (1987), 94(3), p. 315-35</ref> These compounds, based on [[Zirconium tetrafluoride|zirconium fluoride]], unknown until now, attract the attention of the [[Optical communication|optical telecommunications]] world because of their potential for ultra-transparency.<ref>Lucas, Jacques, « Fluoride glasses for modern optics », ''Journal of Fluorine Chemistry'', (1995), 72(2), p. 177-81</ref><ref>Jacques Lucas, « « Fluoride glasses », Current Opinion in Solid State », ''Science'', 2, 1997, p. 405-411, 181-187</ref> Developed in the form of fibres, their wide optical window 0.4 to 7 micrometers (μm) gives hope for an area of very low optical losses estimated at 0.02&nbsp;dB/km. These glasses contain [[Rare-earth element|rare earths]] as constituent elements.<ref>Lucas, J.; Adam, J. L., « Fluoride glass optical waveguides for rare-earth-doped devices », ''Optronics'', (1995), 167, p. 121-6</ref> Doped fibres have thus been developed for the production of laser fibres or optical amplifiers. He then began to look for other glasses containing much heavier atoms based on [[tellurium]]. In collaboration with Zhang,<ref>Lucas, J, Zhang, X. H., « The tellurium halide glasses », ''Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids'', (1990), 125(1-2), p. 1-16</ref><ref>Lucas, J., « Recent progress in halide and chalcogenide glasses », ''Solid State Ionics'', (1990), 39(1-2), p. 105-12</ref> he discovered TeX lenses (X= Cl, Br, I). These lenses transmit light up to 20&nbsp;μm.<ref>Jacques Lucas, « « Infared Glasses », Current Opinions in Solid State Materials », ''Science'', 4, 1999</ref><ref>Lucas, J.; Chiaruttini, I.; Zhang, X. H.; Fonteneau, G., « Materials Tellurium halide glasses, TeX glasses, for IR transmission up to 20 micrometers », ''Science Forum'', (1988), 32-33(halide glasses 5), p. 437-40</ref> It recurs with the development of halogen-free lenses in the Te/Ge/Ge/Ga<ref>S.Danto, P. Houizot, C. Boussard-Plédel, X.H. Zhang, F. Smektala, J. Lucas, « A Family of Far-Infrared transmitting Glasses in the Ga-Ge-Te system for Space Applications », ''Adv. Funct. Mater.'', 2006, 16 (14), p. 1847-1852</ref><ref>A.A. Wilhelm, C. Boussard-Plédel, Q. Coulombier, B. Bureau P. Lucas, J. Lucas, « Development of Far- Infrared Transmitting Te based Glasses suitable for carbon dioxide detection and Space Optics », ''Adv. Mater.'', 2007,19 (22) (3796-3800)</ref> system. The development of glasses, in particular their shaping into lenses by a novel moulding process,<ref>Zhang, Xianghua; Ma, Hongli; Lucas, Jacques; Guimond, Yann; Kodjikian, Stephanie, « Optical fibers and molded optics in infrared transparent glass-ceramic », ''Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids'', (2004),  336(1), p. 49-52</ref> led to the creation in the laboratory of a company called Vertex, which became Umicore IRGlass. It is located near the campus. [[Optical fiber|Optical fibres]]<ref>Lucas, J., « Infrared fibers », ''Infrared Physics'', (1985), 25(1-2), p. 277-81</ref> based on tellurium glass have been manufactured and have made it possible to produce [[infrared]] (IR) optical sensors based on the absorption of the [[evanescent wave]].<ref>Keirsse, J.; Boussard-Pledel, C.; Loreal, O.; Sire, O.; Bureau, B.; Leroyer, P.; Turlin, B.; Lucas, J., « IR optical fiber sensor for biomedical applications », ''Vibrational Spectroscopy'', (2003), 32(1), p. 23-32</ref> Many molecules and biomolecules have thus been analysed in situ<ref>X.H. Zhang, B. Bureau, P. Lucas, C. Boussard Plédel and J. Lucas, « Glasses for Seeing Beyond Visible », ''Chem. Eur. J.'', 2008,14, p. 432-442</ref> leading to the creation of a Diafir company created to diagnose biological fluid by infra-red. Micro-structured fibers are also developed in the laboratory and led to the creation of SelenOptics.

== Honours and awards ==
He is the recipient of numerous French and foreign awards:

*    [[CNRS Bronze Medal|CNRS Bronze medal]] (1964).
*    Silver medal from the [[Société des hautes températures et réfractaires]] (1978).
*    Gold medal from the [[Société d'encouragement de l'industrie nationale]] (1980).
*    Prize of the Schützenberger Foundation of the French Academy of sciences (1979).
*    Louis Bourdon Medal for National Industry (1987).
*    Ivan Peychès Prize from the French Academy of sciences (1987).
*    Fellow of the [[American Ceramic Society]] and George W. Morey Award of the American Ceramic Society (1989).
*    Grand Prize for Innovation and Defence (1997).
*    Member of the [[Academia Europaea]] (1998).
*    Grand prix Pierre-Süe de la Société française de chimie (2000).
*    Honorary doctorate from the [[University of Pardubice]], Czech Republic (2000).
*    Member of the French Academy of sciences.<ref name=":0" />
*    Chevalier of the [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'honneu]]<nowiki/>r.
